Whether he had spoken to Mr. Medic telling him that I would arrive and that he was there to liaise with them, that is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have heard all of that several times. I'm asking you more specifically, is it your evidence that commander Trajkovic could not have given them orders?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Trajkovic could not have given them orders unless they were attached to us. Only after their attachment, he would be able to do so. Whether he had an oral arrangement made with Trajkovic, that is something I'm not familiar with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: With Medic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is something I don't know. But without any attachment to the SAJ, orders could not be issued. There was standard procedure that needed to be followed for the SAJ command to assume authority over them as reservists. That is all I know about that. For example, the second time around when they arrived in Kosovo Polje, the procedure was followed and they were properly attached to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You made it clear that Medic had no command authority over them.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, what command authority could he have over them in Serbia as members of the MUP reserve?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You say now that Commander Trajkovic had no command authority.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, Mr. Medic was just another reservist. I didn't know him, and I met him then for the first time. It was for the first time that I could see the reserve unit in Prolom Banja. Before that when Commander Trajkovic told me that he had the right men for us, he just said that he had men whom he had met in a different area. That is all I know. Anything else I would tell you now would not be the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was Medic an officer of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the active or reserve force?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Either.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of the reserve force. As of the moment when they were received individually into the reserve force following minister's orders. Having become members of the reserve force, they were issued with the regular police uniform used at the time and with weapons. They were the MUP's reserve force, as I said in my testimony the day before yesterday. The MUP reserve force could only be engaged following an approval of the minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And Trajkovic could not give them any order?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not before their attachment to the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And Medic was not an SAJ officer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If those two buses on the way to Podujevo had been ambushed by a KLA force, are you saying that there is nobody who could command them? Those reserve force members?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time when they were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No one; is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that is not what I'm trying to say. I really don't know. I never thought about such a situation being possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Right. But you are very adamant that you couldn't have commanded them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could only command them following their attachment to my unit, not before that. I merely followed my superior's orders. He could have ordered anyone else to go and pick them up, and that person would have done the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what authority could he pick them up and bring them to Podujevo if they were not SAJ and not subject to his command?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, on the 27th, before arriving in Podujevo, Mr. Trajkovic went to the staff. He informed them that someone was to go to take them over and that he had been told that there were reservists in Prolom Banja. Had he not been wounded, he would have been the one to collect them after the operation to execute the attachment process to the SAJ command and our units. However, given that the things developed the way they did, on his return, the SAJ commander assigned me the task to do so. The task was not implemented for reasons you are familiar with, the procedure was not followed through, and following my decision to have them returned, I informed the staff because I wasn't able to get in touch with Commander Trajkovic by phone. I informed the sector chief and that is all I could have done under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The assignment you were given by Commander Trajkovic, with respect to these men collecting them as you say, bringing them to Podujevo, you did not see that in any way as giving you authority to command these men?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could only have authority following their attachment because in that case, that reserve unit would have been attached to the SAJ. In absence of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've gone over that same thing. You didn't understand that you in any way were to command these men and bring them to Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On commander's orders, I was merely a liaison officer who was supposed to receive them until the entire procedure is followed through. Had they been attached to my unit, I would have been responsible for them. This is the way I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you can't suggest on what lawful authority Commander Trajkovic could have done what you did? That is, bring the men to Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Trajkovic, even if he had gone to pick them up and had standard procedure been followed, they would have been considered part of the regular MUP force, provided, of course, that the procedure I mentioned was followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not only followed, but completed, as I understand you? It's only after you had finished your coffee, found accommodation, divided up the men between the two units, and reported to the MUP staff in Pristina, only after completion of that would these men have been part of the SAJ unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would have been attached to the SAJ. They would have not been SAJ's reserve force. I've been trying to explain that the SAJ has never had a reserve force. This SAJ, as it exists now even, in Belgrade has no reserve force. We don't have one. Our staffing levels are brought up based on the MUP reserve force numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what basis did you act when you said that the men should stay in the buses in Podujevo on the morning of the 28th? Was that just a social suggestion, or was that an order of a lieutenant-colonel of the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I merely executed the order of my superior, the SAJ commander pending the whole procedure being complete. Before that, they were supposed to stay on the buses so as to avoid any problems. They did not obey --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Was that an order of Commander Trajkovic that they must stay on the buses, or is that something you decided?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was something I told them to do based on my own authority awaiting the completion of the procedure. Had that been done, everything else I have been explaining would have taken place. We would have informed the MUP staff that things were in order and that the reserve force members were attached to the SAJ and that as of that moment they were under our command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, there's one matter I haven't asked. Are you saying that there had been no arrangements made to accommodate this force of over 100 men in Podujevo before they arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire SAJ command with both units in the afternoon on the 27th arrived in the area of Podujevo. We had difficulties finding accommodation ourselves. Once they arrived they were supposed to stay on the buses until such time when accommodation was found for them. I have explained why, we tried to find accommodation close by so that they wouldn't disperse and that proper security measures were followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, I just have one inquiry to make. Now, in answer to Judge Parker awhile ago, you said that the first day, you said that the first day that Commander Trajkovic directed you to find Medic who was the contact person for the reserve men, the liaison? Did you tell that to Judge Parker awhile ago?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told His Honour that Commander Trajkovic told me that once I was in Prolom Banja to seek out Mr. Medic and get in touch with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: He was the contact person?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I was told by my commander, Mr. Trajkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to direct your mind to the evidence you gave on that first day, and I shall read it for you: "When I arrived in Prolom Banja, I was instructed by Mr. Trajkovic to look for a certain Boca, his name is Slobodan Medic. And that he was with this reserve force of the MUP but that in an oral agreement between him and Mr. Trajkovic he was in a way responsible for them, for this force." Do you recollect saying that on the first day?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I did say so, then I have no reason to question what you have just said. I wasn't trying to hide anything. This is what I was told by Commander Trajkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: No, no, the question I'm asking you now, and I would like to hear from you, when you say he was in a way responsible for this force, what do you mean by in a way responsible for this force?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant what I said, that he was the contact person. Whether he had any arrangements with the command, that is something I don't know. But I didn't mean to suggest that he commanded them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I see. When you say responsible, you mean he was the contact person?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Simovic, I have another question related to the question of finding accommodation. What did you have in mind when you ordered your unit to find accommodation? How could that happen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I refer to finding accommodation, my men, that is to say, active duty members of the SAJ, since the bombing campaign was already underway, and given that many Serbs and Albanians who lived in Podujevo had left because of the danger of being bombed seeking shelter with friends in safer areas, hence there were empty houses there. I had in mind that they should find empty houses where there were no occupants at the same time trying to stay together in one location. We couldn't accommodate all of them in Podujevo though because any MUP facility would have become a target, hence we could not accommodate them there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What was your estimation how many days you would stay in this area with your unit?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN SIMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. It turned out that on the 28th, the rest of the unit left Podujevo. One never knows. That very much depends on the subsequent task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unusually, the Chamber has asked a number of questions of the witness. Mr. Stamp, is there anything that you would want to ask arising from what the Chamber has asked?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never after your questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will be pleased to know, Mr. Simovic, that that concludes the questions for you. We would thank you for your attendance and for your assistance, and you may, of course, now return to your normal activities, and a Court Officer will assist you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you for the patience you exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it pleases, Your Honours, there's the outstanding matter I'm just reminded of the document 0611.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There had been an issue as to some of the pages and, in fact, there were some pages which did not belong, which have now been removed from the document in e-court, so I ask that it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So this now is something that's done by arrangement with Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not so. I see he shake his head but very sternly. So I will turn to Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We stopped when Mr. Stamp introduced a document. I objected then waiting further use of the document, but Mr. Stamp did not put questions to the witness concerning the document today. First of all, that document has nothing to do with the witness, and the witness cannot confirm any of its contents. That was the basis of my objection, and I believe it could not be admitted on that basis. The second thing is that the contents of the document as they are in e-court are incorrect. Only the first two are, whereas the other three have nothing to do with the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to the contents of the document, as in e-court now the contents I see are correct. There was before that an attachment at the end of the document which did not belong to it and that has been removed. In respect to the admissibility of the document, the witness -- although the witness had not seen the document before, this document is a document which on the face of it is a document from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Serbia, the administration for organised crime, and bears the stamp of that ministry, and it relates to an official investigation of that ministry, and an attachment includes a list of the Skorpion unit members. This is an attachment that is referred to at the end of the document, and if one looks at the list, it mentions names of Skorpion members that have been mentioned in court. It mentions Mr. Slobodan Medic at number 1, Mr. Dragan Borojevic at number 14. He is the named accused in the indictment that is before the Court, another exhibit, number 43, Dejan Demirovic, another Skorpion member whose name the witness has testified to. Zeljko Djukic at number 49. At number 65 Dragan Miric [phoen]. Goran Stoparic at number 99 who testified before the Court. Sasa Cvjetan, number 110. So the document not only purports on its face and bears a stamp of the minister of interior, it has the indicia -- many indicia that it's a reliable document, and it's an official document from the ministry. The contents of the document, as I indicated in respect to that one attachment, is something that is in evidence, or is corroborated by the evidence before the Court. The other attachments would be the statement of Mr. Zoran Simovic and the statement of Mr. Radislav Stalevic. The statement of Mr. Simovic has already been received in evidence. That is a previous statement that he gave to the investigators, the organisation that was involved in the investigation on behalf of the Prokuplje court in 2001, 2002. And the other statement is a statement of Radislav Stalevic that we propose to tender separately as well in the course of that forthcoming evidence. Probably if the document is brought up, much of what I say would become quite clear. 0611. 06111. So the objection basically is the witness has not accepted some of what was put to him. The main thing that was put to him was that the unit was founded as a volunteer unit and that it was transferred to the reserve formation of the MUP SAJ with the approval of General Djordjevic. However, there are other elements of this document, which is supported by the evidence, even the evidence of Mr. Simovic as to what happened at Podujevo, and the document on its face is -- and based on the representations I have, is an official document from the administration for the prevention of organised crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is a July 2001 document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. It is the 11th of March, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I had indicated earlier that the date is on the official, to the left of the official stamp in the original B/C/S document but for some reason it was omitted from the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the nature of the document is a request from the administration for the prevention of organised crime to the district court, to a district court requesting an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is a report from the administration for the prevention of organised crime to the Prokuplje district court to provide information to the court in respect to the investigation which the court was then conducting. And these are investigations that the witness testified about and referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So this is the actual response of the ministry's organised crime administration?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To a request from the court?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From the court, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, were you going to go to attachments or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. The only attachment on the document, if we look at the third page of the document of the English, it refers to three attachments, four attachments. One of the attachments is the statement of Zoran Simovic was used with the witness and was tendered separately. The next attachment of statement of Radislav Stalevic, we propose, depending on whether it becomes relevant for the purpose of cross-examination, to tender that later on. And so -- and there's a third attachment of the statement of Srdan Manojlovic, which we don't propose to tender at this stage but we tender if becomes relevant depending on the cross-examination of the witness Stalevic. So the only other attachment is a list of Skorpion members, and that is attached to the exhibit as it is now in court. So if we move to the next page of the document in both English and B/C/S, we would see the list of the Skorpion members, and it lists in four pages 130 of them. One could see that the first name on the list is Slobodan Medic. Number 14 is Borojevic, as I indicated. So this list is quite consistent with the testimony of the witness, that these were members of the group. I won't go through it, but there are names that the Court will quite readily recognise as members of the group. One of them did testify before the Court. So this again supports the authenticity of this document. What had happened is that there was an additional document that had been attached to the exhibit which did not belong as part of the exhibit, and that additional document has now been removed, so the only attachment on the exhibit as it is now is the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it is the Prosecution's submission that this should be admitted for proof of its contents, not merely as proof of the fact that there was such a report made?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As proof of the fact of the report and as proof of the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Of course -- thank you very of, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there anything further, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I -- there is. Overnight without prior notification to the Defence, the document that is not contained as an attachment was removed. Second, apart from the first page of the document, and none of it is confirmed by the witness, the list that follows what Mr. Stamp is showing now has not been shown to the witness at all, and he made no comment at all. All the comments he made were to the effect that he doesn't know what they were doing and how they were doing it. That document has been known to the Prosecution for a long time. There have been other witnesses to whom this document would have been familiar. On the other hand, if there had been any mention of this at the outset, that is at the beginning of today's session, we have another document of this kind that is regularly on the 65 ter list under the number 05220, it contains certain information that this document does not, and I would have presented it. And I would have had questions to put to the witness about it. If the intention is to admit the document through this witness, I would have certainly had questions. But since the witness knows nothing about this document, he was unable to confirm anything, and now Mr. Stamp is mentioning a list that has not been shown to the witness at all. As for what was shown, the witness said I have no idea about this. So if the witness is still here and if you intend to have the document admitted, then I would kindly ask you to bring the witness back to let me show him the document that I have that contains very relevant points, the contents is almost the same but a bit more complete. However, this document that the Prosecution introduced subsequently, 0611, I don't see any reason why they are trying to have it admitted now. We have a similar document in a different version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the view of the Chamber, Mr. Stamp, the document should not be received. The document may be an official document, and that is it's apparent condition, but no witness has been able to speak to the reliability or truth of the contents of the document, and no witness has spoken about the list and the second and third statements, which are said to be attachments to it, and as you have indicated, the other attached statement is separately and properly already an exhibit. So in the Chamber's view, it would not be in the interest of justice in this case to receive this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours. Could it be marked nonetheless?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It certainly can be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01596 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In view of the time, that seems a convenient moment for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours. But there's another thing that was -- I was a little bit remiss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you got another procedural matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: A very important procedural matter, Your Honour. I should have introduced to the court Ms. Jessica Jones, who is assisting the Prosecution with these two witnesses. I was a little bit negligent earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We also welcome Ms. Jones, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the adjournment now and resume just before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, your next witness is.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stalevic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Will you please read aloud the affirmation that's shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, I think Mr. Popovic has some questions for you. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stalevic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stalevic, before we begin with the examination, I will ask you since we both speak the same language to hear out each of my questions and then only begin with your answer to facilitate the work of the interpreters. Can you tell us your name? Your full name.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Radislav Stalevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When were you born and where?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 20th October, 1961 in Babici village, Pec municipality in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you a member of the Ministry of the Interior, and if so, since when?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: I've been a member of the Ministry of the Interior since 1981 when I began to work there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly about the positions you occupied within the Ministry of the Interior in your career?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: When I finished primary school, I went to the secondary school of Internal Affairs in Vucitrn, and after graduating, I began to work as a police officer in OUP, the police department of Djakovica. Two months later in 1981, I transferred to the unit for special operations in the provincial secretariat of Kosovo and Metohija, which was just formed. I worked as a police officer until 1983 and then at the proposal of my superior officers, I was sent to the military academy for land forces in Belgrade. I graduated from that academy in 1987 and began to work as an instructor in the school for Internal Affairs in Vucitrn. One year later in 1988, I was transferred from the secondary school of Internal Affairs, I was re-assigned, in fact, to the unit in which I worked before the school, that is the unit for special operations of the provincial secretariat for Internal Affairs as a commander. As the commander. Until 1990, or rather, 1992, I was commander of this unit, and when -- then that unit was taken over by the republic secretariat for Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia. I was then appointed commander of the special anti-terrorist unit, and that unit was based in Pristina. I remained commander of that unit until 2000. After year 2000, I was appointed deputy commander of the special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, the SAJ Belgrade. In 2001, I moved to a gendarmerie unit, and I was assigned as assistant commander of the gendarmerie of the MUP. In 2004 I was assigned to the newly established detachment of the gendarmerie of Novi Sad within the Ministry of the Interior, and I'm still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stalevic. I'd like to go into more detail about your positions and assignments in 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999, I was commander of the special anti-terrorist unit based in Pristina. I was the commander of that special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Before we go further into the organisation of the special anti-terrorist unit, I would like you to briefly describe when this unit was established, how it was established, and how it developed to the best of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: This special anti-terrorist unit, SAJ, was established in 1992 as a special unit for anti-terrorism. It had its base, its seat, and the command of the special anti-terrorist units. That command was in Belgrade at the Ministry of the Interior. And the commander at this command was Zivko Trajkovic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Before you continue with that answer, you told us you were the commander of the unit of the provincial secretariat which was taken over in 1992 by the Ministry of the Interior. Can you clarify that a bit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said already that I began to work as a police officer in a special unit, in fact, a unit for special operations which belonged at the time to the province secretariat. And after finishing the school that I mentioned, I was appointed commander of that unit in 1998. More exactly, on the 14th of June, 1998, when I received my letter of appointment from the then-provincial secretary Rrahman Morina.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Which year was that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: 1988. The 14th of June, 1988. That was the day when I received my letter of appointment and began to work. Later on that unit for special operations did not function within the MUP. It was a provincial province unit. In 1990 when the police officers, and there were Albanians, Montenegrins and Croats, et cetera, when all of them or most of them left the unit in 1990, the unit continued to operate with a smaller number in 1992. It was still at that time the unit of the province secretariat, and in 1992, it became part of the republic secretariat of Internal Affairs. It became part of special anti-terrorist units.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stalevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To clarify a bit further the mode of operation of this unit, I'd like to call D401.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This document will appear on your screen, and I will put to you you some questions related to the document. Mr. Stalevic, this document is dated 5 April 1996. It's a decision establishing special anti-terrorist units adopted by the then-minister Zoran Sokolovic. In item 1 of this decision, it says that special anti-terrorist units are hereby established as separate units of the public security sector of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia with headquarters in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina. Could you give us a brief comment.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: I can't see much on the screen. I don't know if we could make the letters larger. Yes, I can see, paragraph 1, that special anti-terrorist units are established with headquarters in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Were there indeed units in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and Pristina?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these three units existed. One in Novi Sad, one in Pristina, one in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You were commander of which one?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: As I said earlier, I was commander of the special anti-terrorist unit in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Who is the commander of the entire special anti-terrorist unit in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the special anti-terrorist unit in 1998 and 1999 and earlier was Zivko Trajkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: How many men did the SAJ Pristina number?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: The SAJ had around 100 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many members the other two units, the one in Belgrade and the one in Pristina had? You can give us a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: We had approximately the same number of men, about 100 men. The Belgrade, the Novi Sad, and Pristina units.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So how many men in total did the entire special anti-terrorist unit have?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Around 300. 100 per unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And the command of the entire special anti-terrorist unit was where?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: The command was in Belgrade in the Prince Milos Street where the Ministry of the Interior building is as well, and among these 300 men, we also had each one deputy commander, one analyst, and a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now look at paragraph 2 of this decision. I don't want to read it, it's a long paragraph. You can read it for yourself. Those are the tasks and duties of the special anti-terrorist units. Just tell us whether they are correctly listed, whether these were indeed the duties of special anti-terrorist units?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these were the tasks and duties of special anti-terrorist units.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How was a special anti-terrorist unit organised? What did it have within its complement that is stipulated in paragraph 3, but I suppose you can describe it briefly?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: My special anti-terrorist unit, SAJ Pristina, had a command and three platoons. In the command of each unit, there was a command deputy, assistants, the record keeper, a physician, and a driver. There were also platoons. The 1st Platoon in the SAJ was a close quarter combat platoon, and the 2nd Platoon was a support platoon. The 1st Platoon had 30 men, the 2nd also around 30 men. And the 3rd Platoon was a security platoon practically a technical service, so the total number was 100, 105 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, turn to the next page of the document, please, in both versions. And I'll ask you, Mr. Stalevic, to look at paragraph 7. Paragraph 7 reads: "With the adoption of this decision, the decision of the Ministry of the Interior number 1752/92 of 30th June, 1992, and DT 01 number 4185/93 of 1st January, 1994, I rendered null and void." Tell me, did these decisions mentioned here have any relevance to the special anti-terrorist units, and what?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these decisions were in place and the special anti-terrorist unit existed in 1992 and the decisions made in 1992 were rendered null and void when the new decision was made in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: All right. What were your powers as the commander of the special anti-terrorist unit Pristina?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by "powers", competencies?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: What were your powers regarding this SAJ Pristina?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of that unit, the SAJ Pristina unit. I conducted training for police officers in that unit. I trained, commanded, and controlled them in all our duties and tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Who decides about the engagement, the employment of a special anti-terrorist unit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Decisions about the employment of a special anti-terrorist unit are made by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And who was your direct superior who issued you with orders in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999 I and my unit were directly subordinated to Commander Zivko Trajkovic who issued me with orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know who gave orders to Zivko Trajkovic regarding anti-terrorist actions that the unit carried out in Kosovo and Metohija in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: I do know. I do know about 1999. Commander Trajkovic received his orders for the staff for the combat against terrorism of the province of Kosovo and Metohija, that was the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the staff for combat against terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. Where do you get your knowledge about the activities of that staff in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the latter half of 1998 Commander Trajkovic came to my base, the base where we were stationed, and that was Ajvalija and informed me that the ministry had set up a staff, a MUP staff for combat against terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija, and he informed me that he learned the staff was headed by Sreten Lukic and David Gajic. He too was a member of the staff, and Milorad Legija was the commander of the unit for special operations. Milorad Lukovic, also known as Legija.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So did Zivko Trajkovic specifically receive orders for anti-special operations from the MUP staff for Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that your unit was directly subordinated to the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija when executing anti-terrorist operations in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: At that time our unit was subordinated to the staff for combatting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say it was subordinated to it, could you please clarify. First of all, do you know in what way Zivko Trajkovic received his orders from the staff for combatting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Zivko Trajkovic was a member of the staff. Whenever he returned from the staff to the command in Ajvalija, he brought excerpts from topographic maps, and he would acquaint me and Simovic with the axes and movements necessary to be made in the course of the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Was such a topographic map excerpt the only thing you could see on such occasions?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: As I said, I was shown only the topographic maps excerpts.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how Trajkovic received such excerpts, if you know, of course?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Such excerpts needed to implement operations were given to Trajkovic directly. Or someone would bring them from the staff to him. In other situations he could also send a courier to pick up such an excerpt from the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stalevic, after operations were completed, did you submit reports, and if so, to whom?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: After operations were complete, we always conducted analyses with our commander Mr. Trajkovic. On such occasions we pointed out any problems we had in the course of the operations, and then he, in turn, informed the MUP staff for combatting terrorism in Pristina about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In order to provide a more comprehensive answer, did you submit any written reports to Commander Trajkovic concerning your operations?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. We only conducted analyses, and the commander submitted reports to the MUP of Serbia staff in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Commander Trajkovic take part in your operations?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Commander Trajkovic participated basically in all of the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there a difference in organisational terms between the SAJ as it existed in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a difference. In 1998 in the special anti-terrorist units of the Ministry of the Interior, well, there were three such units; the one in Novi Sad, the one in Belgrade, and the one in Pristina. Towards the end of 1998, the minister of the interior, the then-minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic, disbanded the SAJ unit of Novi Sad, hence the difference. Up to that point in 1998 towards the end, we had had three SAJ units with their seats in Novi Sad, Pristina, and Belgrade, and upon disbandment of the third, we were left with only two, the ones in Pristina and Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning the number of unit members, what did that mean in terms of overall numbers? How many members were there in early 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: As I've said already, all the three units were approximately equally strong. When the third unit was disbanded, we had one-third of the men of special policemen less in relation to 1998, which significantly decreased our operational ability, the ability of the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: To be precise in terms of numbers, how many members of the SAJ were there in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 we had a number of casualties, those wounded and killed. The number was between 50 and 60. Similar to the number of the unit of the Belgrade unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: How many approximately would that be?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we had between 100 and 110 that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: As opposed to the 300 back in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 there had been 300. And when that unit was disbanded, the two units were left with about 100 men each in 1998, which significantly decreased our operational ability.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: When speaking of those remaining in early 1999, were you able to efficiently meet the requirements posed before you with the number of men you were left with?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: Given that our operational ability decreased, we had great difficulty in responding to the requirements and tasks put before us in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any reservists in your SAJ unit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: No. An SAJ unit never had its reserve force. People are selected individually to the SAJ. They are cherry-picked from schools and active-duty personnel, and we never had a reserve force as a unit. We never had any reserve force of the SAJ since it was an elite unit, and as such, it could not have reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were any additional tasks issued to the SAJ in early 1999? Did you have any such information, or were you informed about it, were you ordered to do something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: In early March at one of the meetings I attended alongside Simovic, Zivko Trajkovic informed us that he had attended a meeting in mid-February when Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic attended as well. He required that the SAJ be more engaged and more involved because by that time the NATO aggression was looming. He informed us that given -- that our operational ability was reduced, we were supposed to come up with a reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When Zivko Trajkovic informed you of the need of this greater engagement, did he also propose how to deal with the situation especially in view of the fact of the number of people you had?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, he told us that he would see to it that a reserve force be found. Indeed, later on he told us that he had spoken to Mrgud whom he had known from Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Sermia [as interpreted] about that reserve force. Apparently Mrgud told him he knew of the people who could make part of that MUP reserve force. After that, Trajkovic informed the chief of the sector about the fact that he located a number of reservists who could be made part of the unit. He also said that Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic, the sector chief, told him that the minister's decision still awaited on the issue of joining the MUP by the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said this was in early March. What was otherwise regular length of time one would need to become a member of the SAJ, say, in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: As I've already said, I believe, those people were screened. We had very good co-operation with the interior high school in Sremska Kamenica and the best and ablest men were chosen from that high school. They were either assigned to various secretariats and SUPs, and then in time we would test them as the best. We would test their physical prowess and carry out medical checks to have them selected. The process lasted quite a while, but at that point in time, we could not embark such a process in view of the looming NATO aggression. It was expected, not necessarily looming, but we believed it would take place nonetheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that he had spoken with someone named Mrgud who told him he knew of some men who could comprise a reserve force of the MUP. Did Zivko Trajkovic tell you whether he personally knew any of those people Mrgud referred to?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC
utterances.text: In Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Sermia [as interpreted] in 1992, Trajkovic was there in the area. He knew Mrgud as well as a number of other people, probably some of those who were to be included into the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, we seem to have two minutes left, and I'm about to embark upon a lengthy topic. Do you think it would be better to stop now, otherwise I can go on, if you deem it necessary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now, Mr. Popovic. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. A Court Officer will assist you during the break. We resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
